title: Startrails over the Atacama
caption: Star trails over the Atacama Desert, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars sweep in circles around a point on the left side of this picture, taken looking south over Chile's Atacama Desert. That point is the celestial south pole. The image was made from a long series of night-time exposures by Babak Tafreshi.

The circles are the result of Earth's rotation. As the planet spins on its axis, the sky appears to turn around the celestial poles, the points directly above Earth's own poles. Stars near the south pole trace tight rings, while stars farther away sweep out wider arcs.

Individually, each exposure shows stars as points. Combined, the frames link those points into trails. Looking south from the Southern Hemisphere, the pattern is centered on the pole, but no bright star marks that spot, so it shows up only as the hub of the circles.

understand.summary: This is a series of night-time photographs taken in visible light with a camera in the Atacama Desert and combined into one image. The exposure settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. Only by combining many exposures can a camera show them circling the pole.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture looks south over the Atacama Desert, where, as for anyone in the Southern Hemisphere, the celestial south pole is always above the horizon.
alt: Circular star trails centered on a point at the left of the frame, above a desert landscape.
